walkthroughs.body_html:
The UK is religiously diverse. The 2021 Census recorded around 46% Christian and 6% Muslim, with about 37% saying 'no religion'.

Multicultural means many cultures live together; multi-faith means many religions coexist.

Religious freedom is protected by the Human Rights Act 1998 and Equality Act 2010.

Prejudice is what you think — judging someone before knowing them.

Discrimination is what you do — treating people unfairly based on prejudice.

Forms include racism, sexism, ageism, religious discrimination and homophobia. UK law forbids discrimination on nine 'protected characteristics' (Equality Act 2010).

Christianity: 'There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 3:28).

Islam: 'O mankind! We created you from a single soul. and made you into nations and tribes that you may know one another' (Qur'an 49:13).

How do samsara, karma and moksha fit together in Hindu thought?
options: Samsara is the cycle of rebirth; karma is the law of action and consequence that drives rebirth; moksha is liberation from samsara — these form a connected chain, not three independent ideas.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Samsara, karma and moksha are three separate Hindu deities.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was half God and half human.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.

mcqs.q: What is distinctive about the ontological argument?
options: The ontological argument uses scientific evidence to prove God exists.
Moksha is the Hindu word for heaven.
It tries to prove God's existence purely from the concept of God — a priori reasoning needing no empirical evidence about the world.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
